l-m-e5-b02-05.material: Claim: Line-symmetric figure always get only one line of symmetry. For sans-serif letters A, T, H, Y, find the letter wey show say this claim no correct.

l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose the two fractions wey go against the claim (na counterexample).
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s1.r.a: 1/3 big pass. The sizes no be the same, so this one na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s1.r.c: Dem be 14/35 and 15/35, so the sizes no be the same. This one na example wey fit the claim.
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s1.r.d: The denominators be the same, so dem no fit test the claim.
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s1.explain: If you reduce 3/6 by 3, e become 1/2. Even if the denominators no be the same, the sizes fit be equal.
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s2.model.0: 3/6=1/2, so even if the denominators no be the same the sizes equal, and the claim wrong.
l-m-e5-b03-03.s.s2.model.1: If you multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number, the size no go change even though the denominator change, so 1/2 and 3/6 na counterexample.

l-m-e5-b03-04.s.s1.o.d: A: 30% of 100 / B: 20% of 100 (the two schools)
l-m-e5-b03-04.s.s1.r.d: Dem be 30 and 20, so the one wey get higher percentage get more.

l-m-e5-b01-28.goal: Change the expression for the perimeter of rectangle to another form of expression (expression, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e5-b01-28.material: Dem find the perimeter of rectangle wey be 7 cm long and 4 cm wide with (7+4)×2. Change this expression to another form wey give the same value.
l-m-e5-b01-28.s.s1.prompt: Which expression get the same value as (7+4)×2?

l-m-e5-b01-28.s.s1.r.d: E only add, so e become 13. E no be 22.
l-m-e5-b01-28.s.s1.explain: (7+4)×2=22 and 7×2+4×2=14+8=22. E add the length two times and the width two times.
l-m-e5-b01-28.s.s2.model.1: If you add the two length sides and the two width sides separately, e give the perimeter too, so 7×2+4×2 na the same expression.

l-m-e5-b01-30.goal: Change the condition say the perimeter na 20 cm to another form of expression (expression, table, picture, words), then explain why e mean the same thing.

l-m-e5-b01-30.s.s1.r.a: Product na value wey relate to area. E different from perimeter.
l-m-e5-b01-30.s.s1.r.b: The perimeter na 2 times length+width. The sum na 10.
l-m-e5-b01-30.s.s1.r.d: Multiplication na the expression to find area.

l-m-e5-b01-30.s.s2.model.1: The perimeter get the length and the width two times each, so length+width na half of 20, wey be 10.

l-m-e5-b02-29.goal: Write "to turn average into total sum" another way (equation, table, picture, words) and explain why e mean di same thing.
l-m-e5-b02-29.material: Di average number of books wey 7 people read na 9. Di average na di total wey dem share equally. Make we turn dis statement into di total number of books.
l-m-e5-b02-29.s.s1.prompt: How many books di 7 people read in all?

l-m-e5-b02-29.s.s1.r.d: You divide 9 by 7. You need to multiply di average by 7 to get di total.
l-m-e5-b02-29.s.s1.explain: If di average na 9 books, e be di same as 7 people wey each read 9 books. 9×7=63 books.

l-m-e5-b02-29.s.s2.model.1: Di average na di total divided by di number of people, so if you multiply di average by di number of people, e give di total.

l-m-e5-b03-29.title: Rectangles wey dem make with 12 tiles
l-m-e5-b03-29.goal: Show di divisors of 12 and di shapes of rectangles for another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-e5-b03-29.material: Arrange 12 square tiles without gap to make rectangle. Arrange dem so say di width long pass di height or e equal am. Turn dis one to di language of divisors.
l-m-e5-b03-29.s.s1.prompt: How many different rectangles fit dem make in all?

l-m-e5-b03-29.s.s2.model.1: If you swap di width and height, e still be di same shape, so count 3 pairs, no be 6 divisors.

l-m-e5-b04-06.title: If 8 people share 5 cakes, how much each person go get?
l-m-e5-b04-06.topic: The relationship between fractions and division
l-m-e5-b04-06.goal: Show the quotient of 5÷8 for another form (expression, table, picture, words), then explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-e5-b04-06.material: 8 people share 5 same cakes equally and nothing remain. Write one person share as 5÷8 and talk am again as fraction.
l-m-e5-b04-06.s.s1.prompt: Which fraction mean the same as 5÷8?
l-m-e5-b04-06.s.s1.r.a: Dem write the divisor and the dividend backwards.
l-m-e5-b04-06.s.s1.explain: Dem dey write the quotient of a division with the dividend as the numerator and the divisor as the denominator, so e be 5/8.
l-m-e5-b04-06.s.s2.model.0: 5÷8 na the quotient of 5 divided by 8, so e mean the same as 5/8, with numerator 5 and denominator 8.
l-m-e5-b04-06.s.s2.model.1: When 8 people share 5 cakes, each person get 1/8 of 1 cake 5 times, so e be 5/8.

l-m-e5-b04-22.title: To talk the average as "to share equally"
l-m-e5-b04-22.goal: Change the average of four block towers to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why dem mean the same thing.
l-m-e5-b04-22.material: Four block towers get heights of 3, 7, 5, and 9 blocks. Try talk the average as "the value wey you go get if you move blocks around evenly so that all the heights go be the same."
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s1.prompt: If you move dem evenly, how many blocks each tower go get?
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s1.r.a: Dem calculate only three towers. Dem must use all four towers.
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s1.r.c: Dem decide am from only some of the tower values. Dem must divide the total by 4.
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s1.r.d: This one na the total. Dem must divide am by 4, the number of towers.
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s1.explain: Blocks na 24 in all and towers na 4, so if you share evenly e give 24÷4=6 blocks each.
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s2.model.0: The total number of blocks, 3+7+5+9=24, dem share am equally among the four towers, so the average na 6 blocks.
l-m-e5-b04-22.s.s2.model.1: If you move blocks from the tall towers to the short ones, every tower go be 6 blocks, so e mean the same as the average.

l-m-e5-b04-30.material: Di area of one triangle wey get base of 8 cm and height of 5 cm na 8×5÷2=20 cm². Try connect dis one to one rectangle wey be 8 cm long and 5 cm wide.

l-m-e5-b04-30.s.s1.o.b: E equal di area of dat rectangle
l-m-e5-b04-30.s.s1.r.b: Di rectangle na 40 cm² and di triangle na 20 cm².
l-m-e5-b04-30.s.s1.o.c: E equal one square wey get side of 5 cm
l-m-e5-b04-30.s.s1.r.c: Di area of square na 25 cm², wey different.
l-m-e5-b04-30.s.s1.o.d: E be half of di area of dat rectangle

l-m-e5-b04-38.title: How to write point symmetry again with corresponding points
l-m-e5-b04-38.goal: Change di corresponding points of one point-symmetric shape to another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why dem mean di same thing.
l-m-e5-b04-38.material: One point-symmetric shape na shape wey overlap di original when dem turn am 180° around one point (di center of symmetry). Try write dis meaning again with corresponding points.
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.prompt: Which statement talk di same thing correct?
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.o.a: Di segment wey join corresponding points dey perpendicular to di axis of symmetry
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.r.a: Axis of symmetry belong to line-symmetric shapes.
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.o.b: Di center of symmetry must dey outside di shape
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.r.b: Di center fit dey inside di shape.
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.o.c: Corresponding points dey different distances from di center
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.r.c: Corresponding points dey di same distance from di center.
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.o.d: Di midpoint of di segment wey join corresponding points na di center of symmetry
l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s1.explain: When dem turn am 180°, corresponding points land di same distance away for di opposite side of di center, so di center na di midpoint of di segment wey join corresponding points.

l-m-e5-b04-38.s.s2.model.1: E overlap when dem turn am 180°, so di midpoint of di segment wey join corresponding points na di center of symmetry.

l-m-e5-b05-24.title: Choose shape for pattern card
l-m-e5-b05-24.goal: Consider all conflicting conditions for shape on pattern card, choose best one, and explain.
l-m-e5-b05-24.material: Shape for card pattern must get line symmetry and point symmetry, and have 4 or fewer sides.
l-m-e5-b05-24.s.s1.r.b: E meet conditions, but e get 6 sides, more than square.
l-m-e5-b05-24.s.s1.r.d: E get only 2 lines of symmetry.
l-m-e5-b05-24.s.s1.explain: Square get 4 symmetry lines, point symmetry, and 4 sides, the fewest.
l-m-e5-b05-24.s.s2.model.0: Square get line and point symmetry and 4 symmetry lines, so e meet conditions.
l-m-e5-b05-24.s.s2.model.1: Regular hexagon fit too, but e get 6 sides, so square with 4 sides more suitable.

l-m-e5-b05-32.title: Choose winning rule for dice game
l-m-e5-b05-32.goal: Consider all conditions for winning number in dice game, choose best rule and explain.
l-m-e5-b05-32.material: Roll die once and choose rule "You win if ○ or more show." Conditions: chance win must be more than 1/2 but less than 5/6. (1 3)
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s1.r.a: Chance to win na 4/6, more than 1/2.
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s1.r.c: E meet di conditions, but one rule dey wey get higher chance, 2/6.
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s1.r.d: Di chance to win na 1/6, wey small pass 1/3.
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s1.explain: 4 or more na 3 outcomes, 4, 5, and 6, so 3/6=1/2. 3 or more na 4/6, and 5 or more na 2/6.
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s2.model.0: 4 or more na 3/6=1/2, wey dey inside di conditions, and 3 or more na 4/6, wey pass 1/2, so 4 or more na di highest.
l-m-e5-b05-32.s.s2.model.1: 5 or more na 2/6=1/3, wey dey inside di range, but 4 or more big pass, so 4 or more fit.

l-m-e5-b05-40.title: To cut 2 1/4 m cord without anything remain
l-m-e5-b05-40.goal: Think about all di conditions wey dey clash for how to make up di pieces wey dem cut from cord, choose di compromise wey fit pass, and explain why.
l-m-e5-b05-40.material: You go cut 2 1/4 m cord completely, without leaving anything. Di only pieces na 1/2 m pieces and 3/4 m pieces. Condition: as many pieces as possible.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.prompt: Which way to cut fit di conditions best?
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.r.a: Dem use only 2 m and 1/4 m remain.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.r.b: Nothing remain, but only 3 pieces dey.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.o.c: 3 pieces of 1/2 m and 1 piece of 3/4 m
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.o.d: 2 pieces of 1/2 m and 2 pieces of 3/4 m
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.r.d: Di total na 2 1/2 m, wey long pass di cord.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s1.explain: 1/2×3+3/4×1=9/4=2 1/4 m, so e use am finish with 4 pieces. If you use only 3/4 m pieces, e give 3 pieces.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s2.model.0: 3/2+3/4=9/4=2 1/4 m, so nothing remain and 4 pieces na di most.
l-m-e5-b05-40.s.s2.model.1: 3 pieces of 3/4 m use am finish too, but na 3 pieces dat one, so di option wey get 4 pieces fit pass.

l-m-e5-b0s3-08.title: To fill bottle with juice and milk
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.goal: Think about all the conditions wey dey fight each other for filling bottle with juice and milk, choose the best compromise, and explain why.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.material: Pour at least 3/4 L of juice and at least 1/2 L of milk. The total must no pass 1 1/2 L, and among the plans wey follow the conditions, the total must be the largest.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s1.prompt: Which plan follow all the conditions and get the largest total?
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s1.r.a: The total na 1 1/4 L, wey follow the conditions, but one plan dey wey pour more.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s1.r.b: The total na 1 7/12 L, wey pass 1 1/2 L.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s1.explain: 5/6+1/2=1 1/3 L, the largest among the plans wey follow the conditions. 5/6+3/4 pass 1 1/2 L.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s2.model.0: Juice and milk each reach the minimum, and the total 1 1/3 L no pass 1 1/2 L, so na the best plan.
l-m-e5-b0s3-08.s.s2.model.1: 3/4+1/2 na 1 1/4 L, wey small pass, and the others break one condition, so 5/6 and 1/2 na the best.
